sources.entry: prophet - A tool for producing forecasts for time series with multiple seasonality and trend changes.

summary.one_liner: Prophet is Facebook's open-source procedure for forecasting time series, using an additive model with trend, yearly/weekly/daily seasonality, and holiday effects.
summary.what_it_does: Fits an additive model in which non-linear trends are combined with yearly, weekly, and daily seasonality plus holiday effects. The README says it works best with time series that have strong seasonal effects and several seasons of historical data. It is described as robust to missing data and shifts in the trend, and as typically handling outliers well. It is distributed as an R package on CRAN and a Python package on PyPI (also via conda-forge). The changelog mentions cross-validation, custom seasonalities, extra regressors, saturating growth, country holidays, and performance metrics. A separate Scala/Apache Spark reimplementation called Helter Skelter, maintained by Amadeus, is also mentioned.
notable: Additive model with automatic yearly, weekly, and daily seasonality plus holiday effects
Available in both Python (PyPI, conda-forge) and R (CRAN)
Helter Skelter Scala/Spark reimplementation for distributed computing
Robust to missing data and trend shifts according to the README
caveats: Version 1.4.0 and later are in maintenance mode: only bug fixes, dependency bumps, and R/Python parity changes; no new features are planned
The CRAN version is described as outdated; the README recommends installing the latest release from GitHub
On Windows, a C++ compiler toolchain (such as Rtools or mingw-gcc) is required; Linux needs at least 4GB memory to install and 2GB to use
